gloss: to have a point; to make sense

definitions.gloss: to have a point; to make sense; to be reasonable
definitions.explanation: Acknowledges that someone's opinion or argument has some merit or logic to it, even if one does not fully agree. Literally means 'there is one reason/logic.' Composed of 一 (one) + 理 (reason) + ある (to exist).

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{意見|いけん}にも{一理|いちり}ある。
examples.english: His opinion has a point too.

examples.japanese: たしかに{一理|いちり}あるが、{賛成|さんせい}はできない。
examples.english: It certainly makes sense, but I can't agree.

examples.japanese: その{考|かんが}え{方|かた}にも{一理|いちり}あると{思|おも}わなくもない。
examples.english: I can't deny that way of thinking has a certain logic to it.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used to partially acknowledge an opposing viewpoint before stating disagreement: 「{一理|いちり}あるが…」 (You have a point, but...). The expression conveys measured, rational assessment rather than enthusiastic agreement.
This expression sounds thoughtful and balanced. It is commonly used in discussions and debates to show fair-mindedness.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～にも{一理|いちり}ある (... also has a point)
- たしかに{一理|いちり}ある (it certainly makes sense)
- {一理|いちり}あるが (you have a point, but...)
